content:
Thoughts on Sharjeel Imam and Freedom

Following is a seven panel series illustrating the author, Firaaq's thoughts on Sharjeel's return to Tihar, formed from his own experiences in jail (Firaaq was first arrested last year in November during the India Gate protests as a journalist and independent participant, and again this year at the JNU Long March protest in February, again, as a journalist and independent participant). It has been edited and illustrated by Mouli Sharma.

Firaaq is a scholar of human rights and an independent journalist based in New Delhi. His work has appeared in publications like NewClick, GroundXero, and Nutan Charcha.

Mouli Sharma is an independent journalist and illustrator from New Delhi. Her work has appeared in publications like Maktoob Media, GroundXero, The Observer Post, The Leaflet,Nivarana,The Polis Project,Article 14,Feminism in India, and been republished in SabrangIndia, NewsClick andThink Global Health. She is a published photojournalist & illustrator and has been featured in theHindu College Gazette and the quarterly Pink Disco. She is the editor-in-chief of the student-run news site, The Voice Express, and is a literary editor for the digital lit-mag, The Queer Gaze.
excerpt: A seven-panel illustrated essay by journalist and activist Firaaq, written from the experience of his own arrests at the India Gate and JNU Long March protests, on Sharjeel Imam's return to Tihar jail, and what it means to witness the state's appetite for detention from inside a cell. Illustrated by Mouli Sharma.

related.title: Bengal Remembers: Sengar, Epstein, and RG Kar's Legacy on International Women's Day in 2026

related.excerpt: A photo essay from the 52nd New Delhi World Book Fair and its unlikely neighbour, Nakshatra, the trade fair for astrology, tarot, and all things con, held side by side at Pragati Maidan. On the strange coexistence of faith and reason, superstition and literature, in one of the capital's great annual public spaces.
related.title: अंधविश्वास और अन्य बकवास

related.excerpt: A photo essay on autocratic politics and the suppression of thought, the first resource any authoritarian strips from a people is not dignity but the capacity for independent thinking. Photographs and text by Kanika Solanki, journalism student at the University of Delhi.
related.title: Dictate

related.excerpt: A law graduate's account of the 20 July protest against Dharmendra Pradhan at Jantar Mantar: the Delhi Police's lathi charges and a near-fatal stampede, and the protective patriarchy of the men who decided where women belonged.
related.title: Misogyny, Treason, and Plot: Notes from the Cockroaches’ Long Night of Short Knives

related.excerpt: G.N. Saibaba, professor, disability rights activist, and political prisoner, spent 3,592 days in the solitary confinement of Nagpur Central Jail under UAPA charges before dying on 12th October 2024. A tribute and an account of the draconian legal machinery used to silence him, written from outside the gates of JNU.
related.title: “They Don’t Know How to Kill Me”
